On "Cowboys" right now, the most common win still waiting is $5 — 1,117,655 of them on the board — plus ten prizes of $5,000 sitting just under the top end. The full count, top to bottom, is right below. Same time tomorrow — the board will have moved a little, and this page will move with it.
2754.headline: What's actually left to win

2755.body: Somewhere out there, a $100,000 ticket on "Houston Texans" got cashed last week. The board launched with four top prizes and now shows two top prizes — that count is the heartbeat of this page, and it just skipped. Everything below the top tier keeps rolling. The full tier-by-tier count is in the table below — every prize, counted.
2755.headline: The big board just changed

2757.body: Progress report on "Break the Bank": Only a small slice of the tickets have been scratched, putting it early in its run. The part worth watching is the race between the tickets running out and the top prizes running out — right now, the tickets and the top prizes are burning down at about the same pace. If "Break the Bank" is your usual pick, make this page a habit — the board moves even when the ticket art doesn't.
2757.headline: Early innings or late

2764.body: The most interesting number on "Million Dollar Loteria" is the one that hasn't moved: ten of ten top prizes still unclaimed, same as it's been since we started watching it, while the rest of the board keeps paying out and shrinking. Fewer tickets in the stack, same big prizes waiting. That's the free read on "Million Dollar Loteria" for today — every number behind it is on this page.
2764.headline: The waiting game continues

2765.body: Progress report on "Loteria Azul": About three-quarters of the tickets have been scratched, putting it deep into its run. The part worth watching is the race between the tickets running out and the top prizes running out — right now, the top prizes are hanging on while the tickets disappear — the good kind of lopsided. Same time tomorrow — the board will have moved a little, and this page will move with it.
2765.headline: Early innings or late

2768.body: "Lucky 7" just hit Texas stores with four top prizes of $200,000 on the board. A brand-new game is the cleanest look you'll ever get: the board completely untouched, and the printed odds meaning exactly what they say. From here, every day of sales chips away at it — which is exactly what this page tracks. That's the free read on "Lucky 7" for today — every number behind it is on this page.
2768.headline: Fresh game, full board

2769.body: "Lucky 7 Doubler" just landed on Texas counters. Every scratcher starts life as a full board — ten prize levels, all intact with four top prizes of $500,000 on the board — and spends the rest of its run getting picked apart. You're looking at it before the picking starts, which is honestly the cleanest look you'll ever get at it. Every line of Lucky 7 Doubler's prize table below is today's tally, not last month's.
2769.headline: Day one on the shelf

2770.body: Fresh off the truck: "Lucky 7 Tripler", a $20 game from the Texas Lottery with four top prizes of $1 million on the board. Nothing big has been won yet — almost nobody's played it yet. The moment that changes, the numbers on this page will show it. All of it comes straight from official Texas lottery numbers, current through September 9.
2770.headline: New kid on the shelf

2771.body: "Lucky 7 Multiplier" is fresh into its run, with nearly all of its tickets still out there. Games late in their run get interesting when the prizes outlast the tickets; early ones are mostly a bet on the design. Here, neither side of that race is winning right now. The printed odds on the back are truest right now, before the board gets picked over. The full tier-by-tier count is in the table below — every prize, counted.
2771.headline: A progress report
